legalName: Expungement or Sealing Following a Prisoner Review Board Certificate of Eligibility
publicName: Using a Prisoner Review Board certificate to clear a record that is otherwise excluded
mechanism: Two stages before two different bodies. The petitioner first applies to the Prisoner Review Board for a certificate of eligibility for sealing under § 5.2(e-5) or for expungement under § 5.2(e-6); that is discretionary agency relief outside the circuit court. With the certificate attached under § 5.2(d)(2), the petitioner then files in the circuit court under the same venue formula as the pardon route.
exclusions: Stage 2 cannot proceed without the certificate issued at stage 1; the Board's decision is discretionary and outside LegalEase's control.

waitingPeriods.condition: Issuance of a Prisoner Review Board certificate of eligibility
waitingPeriods.duration: None stated for the court stage. The Board controls its own timing.

units.label: Prisoner Review Board certificate application stage
units.description: The participant applies to the Board for a certificate. Which certificate depends on the branch below. Board discretion, the rehabilitation narrative, notarisation, supporting documents and a possible Board hearing are filing instructions and post-generation conditions, not reasons to withhold a packet.

units.label: Certificate of Sealing application, § 5.2(e-5)
units.description: Generate the Board's Certificate of Sealing Acknowledgement and Certificate of Sealing Application from the participant's answers. Both are fillable AcroForms published by the Board, revised 09/18/2024. The acknowledgement must be completed first and included with the petition or the petition is rejected and returned. Rehabilitation, personal-history and reasons narratives are participant-authored through structured prompts, and the perjury declaration is sworn before a notary.

units.label: Certificate of Expungement for Military application
units.description: Generate the Board's Certificate of Expungement for Military Eligibility Acknowledgement and application, v9.18.24. This branch is military-specific and is offered only where the participant's eligibility rests on military service. It is not a general certificate-of-expungement application.

units.label: Non-military certificate of eligibility for expungement, § 5.2(e-6)
units.description: Section 5.2(e-6) refers to a certificate of eligibility for expungement. The Board publishes a Certificate of Sealing and a military-specific Certificate of Expungement; no general non-military expungement-certificate application was located on the Board's site. The filing vehicle for this branch is unverified, so no packet is generated and no form mapping is asserted.
units.unavailableReason: No official non-military certificate-of-eligibility-for-expungement application has been located on the Prisoner Review Board site. The Certificate of Sealing application does not cover it and the military application is expressly military-specific.

units.label: Circuit court petition with the issued certificate attached
units.description: Once the Board issues a certificate, generate the statewide adult Request suite with the certificate attached under § 5.2(d)(2), filed with the Chief Judge of the circuit of conviction, a designated judge of that circuit, or in counties under 3,000,000 the presiding trial judge.

venue: Stage 1 is before the Prisoner Review Board statewide. Stage 2 is before the Chief Judge of the circuit of conviction, a judge of that circuit designated by the Chief Judge, or in counties under 3,000,000 inhabitants the presiding trial judge.

destination.name: Illinois Prisoner Review Board, then the circuit court of conviction
destination.detail: Stage 1 is an agency application. Stage 2 is a court petition with the certificate attached.

selfHelpBoundaries: Stage 1 always: the certificate application is a discretionary rehabilitation case and is not suitable for an automated template.
Any objection or contested hearing at stage 2.
Office of the State Appellate Defender, Expungement Unit, 866-787-1776, is the statewide referral destination for every stop condition.
A Board hearing is a post-generation event. Refer where the Board sets a hearing or where the participant needs advocacy before the Board.
packetInstructions: The Acknowledgement form must be completed before the application and included with the petition, or the petition is rejected and returned.

Notarisation is required before filing: the declaration that all assertions are complete, truthful and accurate must be signed and sworn before a notary public. Perjury is a Class 3 felony punishable by up to 10 years.

Supporting documentation is required before filing and is obtained by the participant: diplomas or transcripts, five years of employment records, proof of completed counselling, a DD-214 where applicable, child-support status where applicable, and any awards, certificates or character letters.

File at least 75 days before the first hearing date on the docket, mail or deliver to the Board at 1001 North Walnut Street, Springfield, Illinois 62702, and send copies to the sentencing or chief judge and the current State's Attorney of the county of conviction with proof of delivery.
No petition will be accepted for review within four years of the denial of a prior petition for the same individual, unless the Chairman permits an exception for compelling reasons.
